title: **Been working on my own TTRPG for a while, finally ready to let people play it**
author: AuraBreakGames
selftext:
Hey guys, I've been working on a high-fantasy tactical TTRPG called "Aura Break" for a while now and finally got an alpha playtest together.

AI was used solely for visually formatting the pages, creating the visual character sheets, maps so that the game could be tested, and combining files into one in a easy to read way. All mechanics, design direction, and creative ideas are from me alone and I do plan to eventually replace all AI generated content if the mechanics are sound and I get positive feedback on the system. 

The basic idea of the game is kind of a mix between 5e + Pathfinder, with AP-based tactical combat, character skill trees, Aura as a resource, and a focus on keeping combat relatively simple while letting characters get pretty deep in how they're built.

I put together a full playtest with pregens, an adventure, maps, GM/player references, and some higher-level boss fights to see how the mechanics holds up. 

Please note that this is strictly a test of the mechanics and not the game as a whole. All names, abilities, scenarios, ect... are meant to be generic and will be changed prior to creating an actual core rule book. 

If anyone wants to give it a shot, here's the playtest:

\[Playtest Packet\](http://files.aurabreakgames.com/AuraBreak-AlphaTest-v0.2.pdf)

And here's the site if you want to see what I'm doing with it:

\[Aura Break Games\](http://Aurabreakgames.com) 

Would honestly just like to see what people think and what breaks once someone other than me gets their hands on it.

comments.author: roach01gt
comments.body: I get that you are developing a game, and you have used AI to help you, but this is by and large a sub for computer games, not TTRPGs. If however you turn your game into a playable version online via something like three js , then you might get some feed back. Otherwise you’re better off looking to subs dedicated to TTRPG for help.
